report: Keine Ödemsignal der erfassten knöchernen Strukturen. Unauffällige Gelenkstellung. Zentrierte Stellung der Patella. Unauffällige Darstellung des retropatellaren Knorpelbesatz des sowie des femorotibialen Knorpelbesatz des, keine Chondropathie. Intakte Darstellung des medialen und lateralen Kollateralbandes. Allenfalls minimale punktförmige flaue Signalanhebung des Außenmeniskushinterhornes (6/21) DD mukoide Degeneration. Des Weiteren intakte Darstellung des Innen- und Außenmeniskus ohne Nachweis einer Rissbildung. Intakter Faserverlauf des vorderen und hinteren Kreuzbandes. Unauffällige Darstellung der Quadrizepssehne sowie Patellarsehne ohne Nachweis einer Ruptur. Unauffällige Signalgebung der umgebenden Weichteile. Gering Gelenkflüssigkeit, kein wesentlicher Gelenkerguss. Keine abgrenzbaren freien Gelenkkörper.

COMPARISON:None.

CLINICAL HISTORY:Right knee lateral joint line pain, locking, giving way. Suspected lateral collateral ligament sprain/meniscal tear. Possible anterior cruciate ligament tear.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the right knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

Extensive multilobulated parameniscal cyst adjacent to the anterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus, measuring up to 42 x 5 x 19 mm in maximum aggregate dimensions. This raises suspicion for underlying horizontal cleavage tear extending through the anterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus. The posterior horn and posterior root are intact. No lateral meniscal extrusion. The medial meniscus is intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

The medial collateral ligament, posterior oblique ligament, fibular collateral ligament, popliteus and biceps femoris tendon attachments, as well as iliotibial band are intact.

The patellar retinacula are intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 11 mm, within normal limits. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

There is mild to moderate patellofemoral chondrosis. Scattered foci of mild chondrosis throughout the medial and lateral femorotibial compartments.

Trace knee joint fluid. Regional musculature is within normal limits. Prominent superficial varicosities at the medial aspect of the right knee and proximal calf. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration.

IMPRESSION:
1. Extensive parameniscal cyst formation adjacent to the anterior horn and midbody of the lateral meniscus raising suspicion for underlying lateral meniscal tear.
2. Intact anterior cruciate ligament.
3. Mild to moderate chondrosis most pronounced involving the patellofemoral compartment, suggesting evolving mild patellofemoral predominant osteoarthritis of the right knee.

In the medial compartment, the meniscus is not torn and there is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
 The lateral compartment, there is suspected small horizontal tear at the body of the lateral meniscus. There is no focal chondrosis or chondral injury. 
 The patellofemoral joint, the patellar and trochlear cartilage appears congruent without chondral lesion. The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact.  
 In the intercondylar notch, there is complete tear of the posterior cruciate ligament, at mid substance. The anterior cruciate ligament is intact. There is no anterior tibial translation. 
 The medial collateral ligamentous complexes are intact. The posteromedial oblique ligament is intact.  
 The lateral collateral ligament complexes are intact. The popliteofibular ligament is intact. The meniscopopliteal fascicles are intact.  
 The extensor mechanism is normal.  
 No knee effusion is present. The surrounding musculature is normal. There is no fracture or bone contusion.   Complete tear of the posterior cruciate ligament, at mid substance.  
  Suspected small horizontal tear at the body of the lateral meniscus.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. Marginal osteophytes are noted at the patella, distal femur, proximal tibia, and intercondylar eminence. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion with synovial proliferation. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: Focal high-grade chondral loss involving the anterior weightbearing portion of the femoral condyle with subchondral cystic changes.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Diffuse high-grade chondral loss involving the median ridge, medial and lateral patellar facets with subchondral cystic changes and reactive edema. Diffuse high-grade chondral loss primarily involving the lateral and central trochlea with subchondral cystic changes and reactive edema.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Degenerative type signal in the MCL without tear. 
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 13 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Severe tricompartmental osteoarthritis primarily affecting the patellofemoral compartment.
2.	Moderate joint effusion with synovial proliferation.
3.	If patient pain persists, geniculate nerve ablation can be considered.

Right knee MRI:

INDICATION: Right knee pain since 4 months refractory to physical therapy. Posterior knee pain.

COMPARISON: Compared to right knee radiographs from [Date].

FINDINGS:
Mild synovitis. Small debris is in the suprapatellar recess and mild effusion. 4.5 x 2.4 x 0.9 cm Baker's cyst.

ANTERIOR COMPARTMENT:
Mild to moderate chondrosis with a focal full-thickness fissure with subchondral bone change at the medial aspect of the lateral patellar facet. Intact extensor mechanism. No significant edema within Hoffa's fat pad.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Moderate chondrosis with area of more than 50% thinning of cartilage. Small medial meniscal body undersurface tear with a flipped fragment in the medial aspect of the medial tibial plateau measuring 7 x 2 mm. Radial tear involving the posterior horn with a flipped fragment towards the intercondylar notch. This fragment measure 8 x 4 mm. Prior healed traumatic injury to the medial collateral ligament proximal attachment.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Mild chondrosis. No discrete meniscal tear. Curvilinear bony fragment overlying the posterior aspect of the fibular head most likely related to a prior avulsion injury of arcuate ligament or fabellofibular ligament. Lateral collateral ligament and biceps femoris appear intact. Iliotibial band appears slightly thickened but without surrounding edema, nonspecific.

INTERCONDYLAR COMPARTMENT:
Anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament are intact.

IMPRESSION:
1. Moderate medial compartment chondrosis with complex meniscal tear described above with a flipped fragment medially to the medial tibial plateau and posterior horn flipped fragment near the intercondylar notch.
2. Mild to moderate chondrosis involving the anterior and lateral compartment. Mild synovitis with debris is in the suprapatellar recess.
3. Remote avulsion injury at the proximal medial collateral ligament and fibular head.

* Wearing of articular cartilage and spur formation and subchondral bone marrow edema over medial tibial plateau, reflecting osteoarthritis.
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar, lateral and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
> A lobulated cystic lesion with internal septumin medial popliteal fossa between the tendons of the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the semimembranosus muscles, in favor of Baker's cyst; mild perifocal edema over medial popliteal fossa.
> The contour of ACL is in a straight line but  increase signal intensity inside, in favor of grade 1 injury
> The contour of PCL appears to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> No evidence of tear is noted in either medial or lateral meniscus.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Subcutaneous infiltration around left knee.
> Heterogenous signal intenisty of patellar cartilage with mild fraying surface, in favor of grade 2 chondromalacia.

Impression: 
1. Osteoarthritis of left knee joint, more prominent at medial compartment.
2. Synovitis of left knee with suprapatellar bursitis and patellar plicae.
3. Baker's cyst with mild perifocal edema.
4. R/O grae 1 injury of ACL.
5. Grade 2 patellar chondromalacia.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

MRI RIGHT KNEE:

INDICATION:    [Age] female with over 6 month history of right knee buckling especially intermittently when doing stairs. No history of trauma or accident. Please rule out intra-articular pathology.

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The extensor mechanism is intact and appears unremarkable.

There is edema seen in the pretibial and prepatellar soft tissues which may correlate clinically with prepatellar bursitis.

The patellofemoral ligaments are intact and appear unremarkable.

There is mild chondral fraying seen to the medial articular facet of patella and there is focal fissuring seen to the femoral trochlear surface of the patellofemoral joint at the apex with intraosseous, subcortical cyst formation. Findings are in keeping with severe chondrosis.

The TT-TG distance is within normal limits at about 5 mm.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

The medial meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment is intact with mild chondral fraying. There is early condylar notch osteophyte formation seen to the medial compartment.

The anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, medial collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament complex including the IT band, fibular collateral ligament, biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon all appear intact and unremarkable.

There is a trace Baker's cyst demonstrated.

There is mild edema surrounding the pes anserine tendons which may correlate clinically with mild pes anserine bursitis.

There is no evidence of a significant knee effusion.

Marrow signal is otherwise normal.

INTERPRETATION: 

Severe chondrosis to the articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint.

Evidence of prepatellar bursitis, mild pes anserine bursitis and trace Baker's cyst.

Additional findings as noted.

No evidence of internal derangement.
